chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Aban, from Al-Sadusi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever comes to me as a visitor, I shall be his intercessor on the Day of Resurrection.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Prophet Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith establishes the spiritual efficacy of visiting the Prophet's tomb as a means to secure his intercession (shafa'ah) on the Day of Judgment. It underscores the enduring bond between the believer and the Prophet, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the physical presence of the Imam or Prophet as a conduit for divine mercy and validation of faith.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Aban, from Al Sadousy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who comes to mesaww for Ziyarah, Isaww shall intercede for him on the Day of Judgement’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Mahbub from Aban from al-Sadusiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Whoever comes to visit me, I will intercede on his behalf on the Day of Judgment.’”
